tendencies.text: Start from cala_facts and the user's own fields; use web research to confirm them or fill gaps, and cite the page you read.
A field you cannot support is null. Mark a field inferred only when it follows from cited facts (e.g. sectors from the product description).
When as_of is given, ignore every fact dated after it, including web pages about later rounds.
On an update, keep every field the update and new evidence do not touch exactly as it was; never drop a sourced field without a change entry that says why.
Rate each part from evidence: fit (clarity of sector and stage), traction (rounds, customers), team, activity (recent rounds or leads); total is the mean of the parts.

Before you use any web page, confirm it is about the same company. Match on more than the name: website domain, country and sector should agree with cala_facts. If a page could belong to a different company with a similar name, leave the fact out and leave the field null. Don't guess.

Turn each cala_facts row into a dataset fact. Keep amount, currency, stage, round_date and investors exactly as given, in the quote and date. Treat 'Not disclosed' as unknown, not as a name. Never make a date more precise than the source: '2025' stays '2025'. Every non-null field must point to fact ids; use inferred: true only for a real inference, such as a stage implied by the round type.

Use the round label from the data to set stage; don't re-label it from round size. Compare the amount with typical ranges (seed about $1.5–6M, Series A about $10–25M). If a 'seed' round is far outside that range, keep the label, mention the gap in the rating reasoning, and use it as evidence of strong traction.

For investors, compute lead_share only from rounds where the lead is actually named, as rounds led divided by rounds with known roles. A lead sets the terms and price and usually writes the largest check. last_lead_date is the announced date of the latest round it led. If there is no lead data, leave both null; never fill them in from mere participation.

Build the rating from parts in [0, 1]: fit, traction (amount raised compared with stage benchmarks), team, and activity (how recent the last round or lead was). Each part must cite fact ids. Score a part conservatively near 0.5 when evidence is thin. When revising a profile, change only fields the update or a new fact supports, and log each change with field, old, new and reason.

notes: Drafted by the training research step from web search. Not validated.
